questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the "oral history problem" in architecture documentation?
options: The reasoning behind a decision exists only in people's memories, and erodes or disappears as the team changes
Architecture diagrams take too long to draw by hand
Terraform state files cannot be stored in version control
Cloud providers deprecate services without warning
questions.explain: The oral history problem is that the context behind a decision lives only in the memories of the people who were in the room, and that context erodes or disappears entirely as people leave or forget.

questions.q: What is "silent reversal," as described in this lesson?
options: A cloud provider silently rolling back a deployed resource
A new or returning engineer removes a piece of complexity because nothing on disk explains why it exists, undoing the constraint it was protecting against
A Terraform apply that silently fails without an error message
An ADR being deleted from the repository without review
questions.explain: Silent reversal happens when an engineer "simplifies" infrastructure that looks unnecessarily complex because no written record explains the constraint the complexity was addressing.

questions.q: Why is "re-litigation" of an already-settled architecture decision expensive, according to this lesson?
options: It always produces a worse outcome than the original decision
It requires purchasing a new software license
It costs real meeting time redebating a question, with no guarantee the second conversation reaches the same already-correct conclusion
It is illegal under most cloud providers' terms of service
questions.explain: Re-litigation burns real time re-arguing a decision from scratch because no artifact exists to show it was already made, and the second round isn't guaranteed to land in the same place.

questions.q: Who is credited in this lesson with describing the Architecture Decision Record pattern, and in what form?
options: Michael Nygard, in a 2011 blog post called "Documenting Architecture Decisions"
A formal ISO standards committee
The original authors of the Terraform CLI
A requirement built into the AWS Well-Architected Framework
questions.explain: Michael Nygard described the pattern in a widely read 2011 blog post, proposing small, dated records of individual decisions instead of documents describing the whole system's current state.

questions.q: What does an ADR actually improve, according to this lesson?
options: It guarantees the original decision was the objectively correct one
It automatically updates infrastructure diagrams when code changes
It eliminates the need for any design discussion before a decision is made
It makes a decision legible to people who weren't in the room, by recording the reasoning, the rejected alternatives, and the accepted tradeoffs
questions.explain: An ADR doesn't make the decision itself better — it makes the decision and its reasoning legible to anyone who wasn't present, including the team's own future self.
